narrative:

Your first-year rank decile was the second most influential factor; you were also in the lowest decile, compared with an accepted-student average of about 6.0, which again increased predicted risk. It was only slightly below the accepted average of 3.23, and it was the one top factor pushing toward passing, but it was not enough to offset the academic-rank concerns. Your LSAT score of 27 is also below the accepted average of 37.18.

To improve your chances if you reapply, focus on raising your LSAT score, strengthening your academic record or adding evidence of readiness for law study, and seek admissions or pre-law advising about how to address the rank concerns. Consider delaying reapplication until you can show meaningful improvement.
